claims.text: 37signals is an American web software company based in Chicago, Illinois, founded in 1999 by Jason Fried, Carlos Segura and Ernest Kim.
It is privately held, and Wikipedia lists 34 employees as of 2021.
Basecamp, the company's flagship project management product, was built out of 37signals' own need to manage client projects when it was still a design firm.
37signals describes itself as having 27 profitable years in business, zero debt and private ownership.
37signals sells web applications under several brands, including Basecamp, HEY, Fizzy and ONCE.
Basecamp charges fixed prices with no per-user fees, and Studio and higher plans include unlimited users.
The ONCE line is sold for one fixed price and is self-hosted by the customer; its first two products are Campfire for group chat and Writebook for publishing a book online.
Ruby on Rails, the open-source web framework created at 37signals, is maintained by a community of over six thousand contributors.
claims.source_title: Ruby on Rails: Accelerate your agents with convention over configuration

claims.text: Basecamp's plan ladder is Free (1 project, 1 GB storage, 5 users), Freelancer at $25 per month, Studio at $59 per month, Pro at $99 per month and Unlimited at $299 per month billed annually.
Basecamp says 2,026 organizations signed up in the last week and offers 10 percent off for registered 501(c)(3) non-profits and free use for K-12 and university class work.
HEY offers a 30-day free trial with no credit card required.
claims.source_title: HEY - A delightfully fresh take on email + calendar, from 37signals

claims.text: ONCE is sold for one fixed price rather than a recurring subscription.
Ruby on Rails was created by David Heinemeier Hansson for internal use at 37signals and publicly released in 2004.
Rails 8.1.4 was released on September 24, 2026.
claims.source_title: Ruby on Rails: Accelerate your agents with convention over configuration

claims.text: Basecamp's pricing page advertises bring-your-own AI agents, CLI access and ChatGPT/Claude connectors with MCP support planned.
37signals closed its long-running Signal v. Noise blog and moved its staff writers to their own HEY World blogs.
claims.source_title: Signal v. Noise is closed. | SvN

claims.text: 37signals maintains a public GitHub organization with open-source repositories including basecamp-sdk, hey-sdk, fizzy and once-campfire.
In 2020 Apple rejected future updates to the HEY iOS app over in-app purchase rules, and 37signals publicly disputed the decision.
claims.source_title: Apple doubles down on controversial decision to reject email app Hey - The Verge

claims.text: 37signals markets Basecamp to bootstrappers, freelancers and small businesses and says it was started without outside funding.
37signals markets ONCE against SaaS subscription fatigue, arguing that customers should pay once and own the software.
Jason Fried is a co-founder and CEO, and David Heinemeier Hansson is a co-founder and CTO; both are listed as key people.
The founding team was Jason Fried, Carlos Segura and Ernest Kim in 1999.
Jason Fried writes publicly on HEY World, where he describes himself as co-founder and CEO of 37signals, makers of Basecamp and HEY.
Basecamp advertises direct access to the CEO via email as part of its customer service.
Cost predictability: Basecamp's fixed prices and no per-user fees contrast with seat-based subscription competitors.
Ownership: ONCE sells self-hosted software for a one-time price to buyers tired of recurring subscriptions.
Durability: 37signals has operated for 27 years, is privately held and carries no debt, which it uses as a trust signal.
Product breadth: an independent company sells Basecamp, HEY, Fizzy and ONCE under one roof.
UNKNOWN: 37signals does not publish revenue, profit or valuation figures, and no reliable public number was found.
